title: Breakout or Temporary Penetration?

stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 2 September 2016. The prior upper zone is highlighted; subsequent candles are hidden.
stages.title: Stage 1 · Before the break
stages.prompt: Look at the earlier highs near the shaded band. What makes this a reasonable upper area to watch, and what rule will you use to call a break?
stages.placeholder: Describe the earlier reactions, state your rule, and name one thing you cannot know yet.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “Price has turned away from this upper area before, so I will use it as a candidate ceiling. For this daily chart, I will count a daily close above the band as a break. Even if that happens, I will not know yet whether price can stay above it.”
stages.selfCheck: A useful response points to earlier highs, states a clear rule (such as a daily close outside), and leaves the later response open.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 15 July–2 September 2016. The shaded 8,810–8,850 band is the candidate upper area. Look at earlier highs near the band; later sessions are hidden.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 chart through 8 September 2016, now showing several closes above the highlighted zone.
stages.title: Stage 2 · Several closes outside
stages.prompt: Compare the latest candle closes with the same band. What has been added to the evidence, and what would still make you reconsider?
stages.placeholder: Say which evidence has been added and what would make you reconsider.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “Several daily closes above the band give the breakout attempt more support than the first crossing alone. My rule has been met, but I still need to see whether price continues to hold outside. A return into the old range would weaken the idea.”
stages.selfCheck: Mention the repeated closes, avoid calling continuation certain, and name a later event that would weaken the reading.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 15 July–8 September 2016. The same band remains fixed; several daily candles have now closed above it. The later sessions are still hidden.

stages.alt: The complete teaching window through 16 September 2016, showing price later returning below the original zone.
stages.title: Stage 3 · Later evidence
stages.prompt: Now compare the final sequence with your first note. Which observations remain true, which interpretation needs updating, and what still cannot be concluded?
stages.placeholder: Keep the earlier closes as facts, then describe the new evidence and your revised view.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “The earlier closes above the band were real, but price later closed back below it and moved into the old range. That weakens the idea that the move was holding above resistance. I cannot say from this chart alone why it failed or that a short trade must follow.”
stages.selfCheck: Keep the earlier evidence, identify the return below the band, update the interpretation, and avoid inventing a cause or a trade.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 15 July–16 September 2016. The original band is unchanged; later price has returned below it and moved back into the earlier range.

quiz.q: A candle wicks above resistance but closes back inside the zone. Which description fits?
options: The session closed and stayed above the resistance zone.
Price traded above, then closed back inside the zone.
The upper band has become support after this first test.
quiz.feedback: The high shows where price travelled during the candle; the close shows where it finished. This is an intraday move beyond the zone, not a close outside it.

quiz.q: One daily candle closes just above a marked area. What can you say now?
options: The session finished above the chosen boundary.
The close suggests buyers kept control into the end.
The close tells us the next session will rise.
quiz.feedback: The close is an observation. It tells you where this session ended, not what the next session must do.

quiz.q: Two closes are above the zone, but later price closes back inside. How would you review it?
options: The earlier closes no longer count after price comes back.
The return proves the zone was drawn too low from the start.
The rule was met, then later evidence weakened the move.
quiz.feedback: The earlier closes remain valid observations. The later return changes the current reading, but it does not create an automatic opposite-side trade.

quiz.q: A chart shows higher volume on both a move that holds and one that fails. What does that suggest?
options: More volume makes a failed move more likely than a hold.
Volume adds context, but does not settle the outcome alone.
Less volume confirms that price will return inside the zone.
quiz.feedback: Volume and price behaviour are two separate clues. Activity can rise in moves that continue and in moves that fail.

quiz.q: A fixed 20-point buffer is used on two different instruments. What is the main concern?
options: The same buffer can mean different things across markets.
The buffer may miss some moves, but works the same across markets.
A fixed buffer matters only after the candle closes outside.
quiz.feedback: Instrument scale and normal price movement differ. A fixed distance is a convention to test, not a universal threshold.

quiz.q: A five-minute break occurs while price remains inside a broad daily range. Which note is clearest?
options: The local break means the daily range has already ended.
The local break is clear; the wider range still matters.
Keep the daily chart for review only if the break fails.
quiz.feedback: Both statements can be true: a local boundary was crossed, while the wider structure remains a range.

quiz.q: Which journal note would be most useful to review later?
options: Strong breakout; I expect price to keep moving higher from here.
Price moved quickly, so continuation seems more likely now.
Close above the zone; reconsider if it closes back inside.
quiz.feedback: A useful note gives the area, the rule, the observation and a condition that would change your view.

reveal: The rule was applied consistently: several daily closes appeared above the chosen band. Later, price returned below it. A fair review keeps both facts and updates the interpretation. The ending was not available at Stage 1.
modelAnswerRubric: Points to price behaviour visible at that stage.
Separates the observation from what it may mean.
Names one uncertainty or alternative path.
Says what new evidence could strengthen or weaken the view.

title: Retests and Role Reversal

stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 14 August 2014, with the candidate former-resistance zone highlighted.
stages.title: Stage 1 · The old upper area
stages.prompt: Look at the earlier approaches to the band. Which reactions support the area, and could another careful reader draw it slightly differently?
stages.placeholder: Point to the earlier highs and say what your band includes.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “Several earlier highs sit near this band, so it is a reasonable candidate ceiling. Another reader might draw the upper edge slightly higher or lower. I will keep this band fixed for now so I can judge the later move fairly.”
stages.selfCheck: Point to earlier reactions, accept that a reasonable boundary can vary, and keep the chosen zone fixed during the first comparison.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 26 June–14 August 2014. The shaded 7,795–7,865 band marks the candidate former-resistance area; later candles are hidden.

stages.alt: The same chart through 22 August 2014, showing the break and a later candle whose low approaches the zone edge.
stages.title: Stage 2 · Price returns towards the area
stages.prompt: Find the bar whose low returns towards the band. Does its low enter, touch or stop short of the zone? Where does that bar close, and what happened after it?
stages.placeholder: Describe the low and close separately; leave the outcome open for now.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “Price has moved above the old area and the later low approaches the band. I will describe the exact low relative to the drawn edge, then check the close separately. This is a return to assess; it does not yet prove that the area is acting as support.”
stages.selfCheck: Describe the low in relation to the displayed band, name the close location, and avoid declaring the retest successful before seeing the response.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 26 June–22 August 2014. The same band remains fixed. The visible sequence includes the move above the area and a return towards it.

stages.alt: The full selected NIFTY 50 window through 18 September 2014, with later price remaining above the candidate area.
stages.title: Stage 3 · Later evidence
stages.prompt: What does the later sequence support in this window? Which claim would go too far—for example, that the band must always hold or that every breakout should be bought on a return?
stages.placeholder: Describe the response, then name one thing the chart still cannot promise.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “In this selected window, price moves above the candidate area after the return, then pulls back while staying above the band. That supports a hold-like reading for now. It does not prove the area will always hold or that every breakout needs a retest. Later price could still return through it.”
stages.selfCheck: Connect the return to the later response, keep the conclusion limited to this window, and mention what could change it.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 26 June–18 September 2014. The same band remains fixed; after the return, later candles move farther above it, followed by a pullback that remains above the band in this selected window.

quiz.q: Price breaks above a range and continues higher without returning. What can you conclude?
options: No return appeared here; a retest was not required.
Without a return, the breakout is still incomplete for review.
A retest is usually needed before a move can continue.
quiz.feedback: Some moves continue without returning. A retest is an additional event to assess, not a step every breakout must complete.

quiz.q: After an upside break, what does “role reversal” mean?
options: The former ceiling can still resist price on a return.
One close above confirms support for future visits.
The old resistance area may now act as support.
quiz.feedback: Role reversal is a possibility to test. Price may hold above the area, cross back through it, or remain mixed.

quiz.q: The wick dips into the band, but the candle closes above it. What should you record?
options: The low places price inside the band for the full candle.
The wick entered the area; the close remained above it.
The zone no longer matters after the candle closes.
quiz.feedback: The low and close give different information. Record both, then look at the later response.

quiz.q: Three later candles close on alternating sides of the band. What is the fairest label?
options: The hold is clear enough to call the role change complete.
The break has changed into a complete reversal now.
The response remains mixed; more candles are needed.
quiz.feedback: When candles keep crossing the band without moving away clearly, the answer is still unclear. You can leave it there for now.

quiz.q: Price closes inside the old range and a later reclaim attempt fails. What changed?
options: The failed reclaim weakens the role-reversal idea.
The boundary must be moved around the newest candles.
The opposite range edge is now the most likely target.
quiz.feedback: Closes in the old range and a failed reclaim are evidence against the idea that the old ceiling is holding as support.

quiz.q: You decide the band needs to be wider after seeing more candles. What is the best practice?
options: Replace the old band after each new high or low.
Keep both versions and record why you revised it.
Choose the wider band because the final chart looks cleaner.
quiz.feedback: A revision can be reasonable. Keeping the old boundary and noting the reason helps you avoid fitting the drawing to the ending.

quiz.q: Which note best describes a return that holds for now?
options: The old area worked, so future visits should hold too.
A long position is justified on the next test of the band.
Price returned, moved away, and stayed above the band.
quiz.feedback: The third note describes the visible sequence and keeps the conclusion limited to this visit.

reveal: In the selected window, price returns towards the candidate area and later remains above it. That supports a hold-like reading here. A different sequence could close back inside the old range or remain mixed; the area does not become permanent support just because it held once.
modelAnswerRubric: Names the original area and how price moved relative to it.
Separates the return (low or wick) from the candle close.
Describes the later response rather than guessing in advance.
Keeps the claim limited and names what could change it.

title: Failed Breakouts and Alternate Outcomes

stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 19 January 2018, showing the candidate former-resistance band before the breakout.
stages.title: Stage 1 · Before the breakout attempt
stages.prompt: Look at the rise into the shaded area. Which earlier highs make it relevant, and what would count as contradictory evidence after a break?
stages.placeholder: State the prior evidence, the boundary you chose, and one possible warning sign.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “Earlier highs cluster near this band, so I will use it as the candidate ceiling. I will count a daily close above it as a breakout attempt. A close back inside the old range, especially if price cannot reclaim the band, would weaken the idea that the move is holding.”
stages.selfCheck: Use earlier candles to explain the zone, state what would count as a break, and describe a future contradiction without assuming it will happen.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 1 December 2017–19 January 2018. The candidate upper area around 10,875–10,920 is shaded; later sessions are hidden.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 chart through 1 February 2018, showing a move above the band and a return that still closes above it.
stages.title: Stage 2 · The return still holds above
stages.prompt: At this point, the close is still above the band after a return. What interpretation remains plausible, and what evidence is still missing?
stages.placeholder: Describe the current evidence and keep at least one alternative open.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “The close remains above the band after the return, so the idea that former resistance may be acting as support is still plausible. I do not yet have evidence of a sustained failure. Later closes back inside or a failed reclaim would change the reading.”
stages.selfCheck: Notice the close remains above, describe role reversal as possible rather than certain, and state what evidence is still missing.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 1 December 2017–1 February 2018. Price has moved above the original band and returned towards it; the relevant close remains above the zone.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 series through 20 February 2018, showing the close below the band and later weakness.
stages.title: Stage 3 · The continuation idea is challenged
stages.prompt: Find the close that moves back below the original band. How does it challenge the continuation idea, and what does it still not prove?
stages.placeholder: Name the close or later response that changed your view; avoid inventing a cause or an automatic trade.
stages.modelAnswer: You could write: “The 2 February close back below the original band contradicts the idea that price was holding above it. Later weakness adds context. The first return had looked acceptable, but the new close changes the reading. It does not prove who caused the failure or mean a short trade is automatic.”
stages.selfCheck: Point to the close back below the band, explain how it weakens the continuation idea, and leave motive and trade choice unclaimed.
stages.caption: NIFTY 50 · daily OHLC · 1 December 2017–20 February 2018. The unchanged band is shown with a later close below it and subsequent weakness.

quiz.q: A candle has just closed above a range ceiling. How should you label it at this point?
options: Price has confirmed a move that should continue higher.
The break has failed before any return inside appears.
A breakout attempt; its next response is unknown.
quiz.feedback: At the first close you can record the attempt. A failure label needs later evidence that challenges the move.

quiz.q: One candle then closes back inside the old range. What does that tell you?
options: The next move lower is now the more likely outcome.
The close now challenges the idea of holding above.
The original zone may have been set too high or low.
quiz.feedback: A close back inside is a clear contradiction to the idea that price is holding outside, but one close does not guarantee the next direction.

quiz.q: After a failed upside break, which paths may still happen?
options: Price may return, move sideways, or reclaim the zone.
Price should reach the opposite edge after a failed break.
Only a strong reversal remains possible from here.
quiz.feedback: Failure makes alternatives worth reviewing. It does not select a single outcome.

quiz.q: For a hypothetical short after an upside failure, which price point matters structurally?
options: Use a fixed number of points above the old zone.
Use the midpoint of the prior range as the reference.
Use the extreme that would challenge the failure idea.
quiz.feedback: The structural reference should relate to the move that failed. It is not a universal buffer or an entry instruction; if the risk is too large, passing may be appropriate.

quiz.q: A market gaps from above a zone to below it. What can the candles tell you?
options: The candle data lets us reconstruct every price inside the gap.
We see the open and range, not the path inside the gap.
The market crossed the gap without any missing prices.
quiz.feedback: The chart does not show trades inside the gap. Describe the prices the data supplies and leave the missing path unknown.

quiz.q: High volume appears during a failed breakout. What does that prove?
options: Volume shows activity, but not who traded or why.
It shows that stops were targeted around the level.
It makes a move in the opposite direction more likely.
quiz.feedback: Volume can describe reported activity, but it does not establish hidden motive or guarantee follow-through.

quiz.q: Price returns into the range, then later reclaims the ceiling and stays above. What should the review say?
options: The earlier return should now be removed from the written record.
The first failure proves any later breakout will hold.
The reclaim adds new evidence against the failure reading.
quiz.feedback: Both events matter. Keep the earlier return, then note that the later reclaim challenges your current label.

quiz.q: A neckline break fails and later candles cross the neckline repeatedly. Which description fits best?
options: The pattern points to a move in the opposite direction now.
The break is not established; the result is still unclear.
The first crossing completes the pattern without more evidence.
quiz.feedback: A pattern name does not settle the result. Repeated overlap can leave the interpretation unresolved.

reveal: The return on 1 February still closed above the band, so a hold-like reading remained plausible at that stage. The 2 February close back below the band then challenged that idea, and later weakness added context. The first view was not foolish; the evidence changed. This does not prove hidden intent or prescribe a short trade.
modelAnswerRubric: Names the boundary and the original breakout convention.
Points to the new candle or sequence that changed the reading.
Explains what the evidence weakens without claiming certainty.
Does not infer hidden motive or turn the failure into an automatic trade.
